issues.description: Constructor parameter list for class Lecture differs between the artifacts. The problem statement requests a constructor that initializes all five attributes in the UML order (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) (problem_statement.md lines 19-21). The solution implementation provides a five-parameter constructor with that exact order (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 13). The template repository, however, contains a constructor with only three parameters (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents) (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 7). This signature mismatch will confuse students about the required parameters and their order and may cause compilation problems or failing tests if automated checks expect the five-argument constructor.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template's Lecture constructor signature to match the problem statement and solution: replace the current three-parameter constructor with a five-parameter constructor in the specified order: public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors) { /* initialize fields or leave TODO body for students to implement */ }. Alternatively, if the exercise intends students to add the constructor themselves, replace the incorrect three-parameter constructor with a clear TODO stub that contains the correct five-parameter signature so students are guided to implement the required constructor in the correct order.
